thread:
deploy-bot: [deploybot] AUTOMATED: Release lane auto-frozen due to elevated DB write error rate in eu-central-1 (ERR-WRITE-117). Holding all deploys and scheduled rollouts in lane 'canary-eu'.
Ravi: saw alerts on writes tripping from app nodes -> db-proxy. thanks deploy-bot. which releases were queued?
deploy-bot: Queued: canary-eu slots 2-4 (versions: v2026.04.01, v2026.04.02), scheduled maintenance jobs at 1725010800.
Noelle: we should avoid forcing retries that could spike connections. ops-sre, can we throttle background requeues?
Amir: on it. pausing requeue workers and autoscalers for the eu cluster. will also hold any DB schema migrations.
Jin: recommend immediate pin to last known-good (v2026.03.28-stable) for canary group until we confirm DB durability.
Ravi: agree. also want to roll back the in-flight deploy that started 1m ago. it's only at 1% traffic.
Noelle: rollback plan (short): 1) set-pin to v2026.03.28-stable; 2) abort in-flight canary job; 3) clear writeback queue; 4) monitor for 20m.
Ravi: executing pin now:
```bash
deployctl set-pin --lane canary-eu --version v2026.03.28-stable --owner Ravi --reason "db-write errors"
```
deploy-bot: Pin applied by Ravi. Auto-requeue disabled for pinned slots. In-flight canary marked for abort.
product-ops-bot: Notifying product and support: "Canary hold in eu-central-1 due to DB write errors. No customer-facing downtime expected. Reschedule ETA TBD."
Amir: aborting canary job and pausing migrator. command: `opsctl job abort --id canary-eu-3`
Jin: once abort finishes, run KV cache linear invalidation and drain writeback queue: 
```bash
infractl kv-invalidate --prefix canary-eu
infractl queue-drain --queue writeback --timeout 300
```
Amir: doing infra steps. will post progress.
Ravi: can we pick a reschedule window now or wait for ops verification? propose pushing the lane +3h and switching to canary-only for 45m, then evaluate.
Noelle: +1 to that window. also add a hard safety gate: if DB write error rate > 1% for 10m, abort rollout. file INF-3189 to track.
Jin: creating INF-3189 (safety gate for DB stability) and linking to release ticket RT-4621.
product-ops-bot: Release ticket RT-4621 updated with hold note and linked incident INF-3189.
Amir: DB proxy errors trending down, current write error pct 0.6% over 10m window. continuing to monitor for 15m. dashboards: https://dash.redwood.internal/db/eu-central-1
Ravi: good. once stable for 15m we should schedule resume but keep the pin until after canary verification.
deploy-bot: Proposed reschedule: canary-eu -> start 1725017789 (approx +3h), canary-only 45m. Manual resume required.
Noelle: schedule that and notify support. ensure release notes say "paused due to DB write instability; rollback applied; reschedule +3h; manual resume after ops okay."
product-ops-bot: Support notified: #support-eu. Release notes snippet added.
Amir: DB stable for 20m now, error rate at 0.2%. ops-sre gives greenlight for manual resume when owners ready.
Ravi: I will not auto-resume. we'll run canary and watch for writeback lag.
Jin: confirm resume checklist: 1) unpause requeue workers in read-only mode; 2) keep autoscaler conservative; 3) enable canary at 2% traffic for 45m; 4) monitor write latency and error rate.
Ravi: ready. initiating manual resume in 2m.
deploy-bot: Resume requested by Ravi. Type `confirm resume` to proceed.
Noelle: confirm resume
deploy-bot: Resuming canary-eu. Canary traffic -> 2% for 45m. Monitoring channels: #db-alerts, #slo-watch.
product-ops-bot: Update to stakeholders: "Canary resumed after DB proxy recovery. Rollback was applied prior to resume; will monitor and abort if errors reoccur."
Ravi: monitoring — write latency stable, metrics look good. closing the hold and logging the actions to RT-4621.
Amir: I'll follow up with the postmortem and include INF-3189 as an action item for a safety gate and smarter requeue backoff.
Jin: adding short ops notes to release ticket with exact commands used.
Noelle: good job team, concise and clean.
